correction: The PARTIAL status holds, but three details in the audit are wrong or imprecise. (1) Web queued sends are mostly covered. ChatView's dispatchComposerSnapshot handles direct sends and foreground queue flushes (ChatView.tsx:4080-4082, 4328-4341), so a queue flush with ChatView mounted already skips the read. Only the headless background sender for an unmounted ChatView (sendQueuedMessageInBackground.ts:160) lacks the reader, and there the thread detail is often not loaded, so the read is often still needed. (2) Remaining item 2 says the reactor already derives the title from titleSeed. It does not. ProviderCommandReactor.ts:360-370 and 1449-1458 use titleSeed only to decide whether an AI-generated title may replace the current one. The decider (decider.ts:1921) passes it through without setting any title. Dropping the first-message thread.meta.update would leave the default title whenever title generation is disabled or fails. Folding it in therefore needs a decider change plus a fallback for older nodes. It also applies only to server threads that already exist with zero messages: draft first sends set the title in the bootstrap thread.create. (3) The web reader takes a snapshot at render time instead of reading the store when the review runs (see fixDefects).
summary: Server half: done. sendTurnOnContext calls setPermissionMode only when the target mode differs from the tracked currentPermissionMode, with semantics unchanged from the old unconditional code. Client half: done only for the web ChatView, both direct sends and foreground queue flushes. When the live subscription clears a send, the getThreadWindow read is skipped, and a flagged send still re-reads server state. Still paying the review round trip on every non-first Claude send: the mobile direct send and the mobile outbox drain (both normally over the hosted relay, both with the detail subscription already retained), the web background (unmounted) queue sender, and the usage-limit 'Resume now' path. Not done: emitting turn.started before the mode switch (the verifier advised against it) and the first-message title RTT (not in the proposal, and harder than the audit says). Minor defect: ChatView's reader closes over render-time state.

evidence.note: setPermissionMode is called only when targetPermissionMode !== context.currentPermissionMode. The tracked mode is set to undefined before the call and to the target after the acknowledgement. claudePermissionModeForInteraction (1630-1637) keeps the old mapping (plan/ask -> plan, default -> base ?? default). Commit c28f9a35a.

A CLI-reported mode that disagrees makes the tracked mode unknown. 5498-5505 does the same for an acceptForSession setMode suggestion. The context is seeded at 5761-5762. ExitPlanMode is always denied (5384-5403), so plan mode cannot leave behind its own back.

When the subscription clears a send, the function returns before getThreadWindow. A flagged send re-reads the server window (activities 40) and reassesses it with the server's workspaceCwd. Tests are at claudeCacheReview.test.ts:302-333. Commit 609ac1563.

The only producer of SubscribedClaudeReviewState. It is gated on live shell plus detail loaded and mirrors resolveThreadWorkspaceCwd (worktreePath ?? project cwd, see checkpointing/Utils.ts:33-49). It closes over render-time activeThread, activeThreadShellLive, activeThreadDetailLoaded and activeProject. dispatchComposerSnapshot then awaits drainEditorsBeforeSend (4109), attachDevicePromptScreenshot (4120) and executeChatSendTurn's uploads and config reads before the review calls it.
Forwards the reader unless a prepared (newly created) thread is the target.

The mobile direct send (called from ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:1349) does not pass readSubscribedClaudeReviewState, so every non-first Claude send awaits getThreadWindow. ThreadDetailScreen already retains the detail subscription (434).

The mobile queued-send drain omits the reader too. createThreadOutboxDetailRetention (around 207-242) already retains detail for queued threads, and selectEnvironmentShellLive and selectThreadByRef are imported (40), so the subscribed state is available.

The headless background sender (used only when no ChatView foreground sender is registered, see messageQueueDrain.ts:50-57) omits the reader. apps/web/src/components/chat/usageLimitBanner.tsx:140-150 via buildUsageLimitResumeDispatch (packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/usageLimitResume.ts:37-77) omits it as well.

The review is awaited first. A first message on an existing server thread still awaits thread.meta.update (380) in parallel with persistThreadSettingsForNextTurn, which only sends the modes that changed (apps/web/src/hooks/chatSendShared.ts:61-98). Then thread.turn.start goes out with titleSeed (446).

canReplaceThreadTitle: titleSeed only gates replacing the title with a generated one (1559, 1449-1458). No code sets the title from titleSeed, so the client's meta.update is what gives the thread its immediate title.

remaining: 1) Mobile parity, the main remaining gain. apps/mobile/src/features/threads/executeSendTurn.ts:151 and apps/mobile/src/state/use-thread-outbox-drain.ts:55 call commitSendTurnDispatch without readSubscribedClaudeReviewState. Every non-first Claude send from the phone, normally over the hosted relay, still waits one getThreadWindow round trip before thread.turn.start, even though both paths keep the thread detail subscribed. 2) Lower value: apps/web/src/hooks/sendQueuedMessageInBackground.ts:160 (unmounted-thread queue sends, nobody watching, detail often absent) and apps/web/src/components/chat/usageLimitBanner.tsx:150 (rare manual resume). 3) There is no shared builder for SubscribedClaudeReviewState: the mapping is inline in ChatView.tsx:4056-4078, so extending it to mobile without extracting it would duplicate logic, against AGENTS.md maintainability. 4) Not done, by design: turn.started is still emitted after the mode switch, which now happens only on an actual mode change. 5) Optional and outside the proposal: the first-message thread.meta.update round trip (sendEngine.ts:376-383). It costs one round trip only on server threads that already exist with zero messages, and removing it needs a server-side title-from-titleSeed change (see correction).
fixDefects: Minor, not a correctness bug in the engine. (a) readSubscribedClaudeReviewState at ChatView.tsx:4056 returns a snapshot of render-time values, not the store at review time. Between the click and the review the send awaits editor drain, the device screenshot, uploads, source-control refreshes and config reads, so it can be judged on a subscription state that is hundreds of milliseconds or more out of date. Examples: a session-set with a new runtimeSessionId, or a context-window.updated that arrived meanwhile. An out-of-date view usually fails toward reading, because an older observation looks more review-worthy. It fails open only when the client lacks the newest observation and the server would flag a settings change. This contradicts the mobile code's own rule to 'read provenance fresh from the store, not from a render' (ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:1319-1323). (b) The gate is 'detail ever loaded' (selectThreadDetailLoaded checks only that history or message ids exist), not 'detail re-synced since the last reconnect'. Just after a reconnect, the shell is live while the activities can still predate the disconnect. Both are narrow advisory cost-guard gaps. The server never enforces a review without a guard (decider.ts:1683 only validates a guard that is present), so a cleared send carries no guard, just as before.
implementationSketch: 1) Add a pure selector in packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeSelectors.ts (or store.ts next to selectThreadByRef): selectSubscribedClaudeReviewState(state: AppState, ref: ScopedThreadRef): { thread: ClaudeCacheReviewThread; workspaceCwd: string | undefined } | undefined. Return undefined unless selectEnvironmentShellLive(state, ref.environmentId) && selectThreadDetailLoaded(state, ref). Otherwise map thread.modelSelection and thread.activities, and map session as {providerName: session.provider, runtimeSessionId (RuntimeSessionId.make when defined), status: session.orchestrationStatus, activeTurnId: session.activeTurnId ?? null} or null. Set workspaceCwd = thread.worktreePath ?? selectProjectByRef(state, scopeProjectRef(env, thread.projectId))?.cwd, treating an empty string as undefined. Export it from @ryco/client-runtime/state/threads; the type comes from @ryco/shared/claudeCacheReview, so no composer-to-threads runtime import is needed. 2) ChatView.tsx:4052-4078: replace the inline closure with () => activeThreadRef && isServerThread ? selectSubscribedClaudeReviewState(useStore.getState(), activeThreadRef) : undefined. This reads the store at review time and fixes defect (a). 3) Mobile: add readSubscribedClaudeReviewState?: () => SubscribedClaudeReviewState | undefined to ExecuteSendTurnInput and forward it in executeSendTurn.ts:151. In ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:1349 pass () => selectSubscribedClaudeReviewState(useStore.getState(), scopeThreadRef(environmentId, threadId)). In use-thread-outbox-drain.ts:55 pass the same for scopeThreadRef(message.environmentId, message.threadId). 4) Pass it from sendQueuedMessageInBackground.ts:160 (useful only when the detail happens to be loaded; otherwise it falls back to the read). Optionally add an optional reader input to buildUsageLimitResumeDispatch and pass it from usageLimitBanner.tsx:140. 5) Optional hardening for defect (b): make the selector also require a per-thread 'detail synced since the last shell snapshot' marker, if the store records one, or clear the detail-loaded state on demotion. Tests: unit-test the selector (shell not live or from cache gives undefined; detail not loaded gives undefined; worktreePath takes precedence over project cwd; session status maps from orchestrationStatus; missing runtimeSessionId is omitted). Add a mobile executeSendTurn test asserting api.orchestration.getThreadWindow is not called when the subscription clears the send and is called when it flags it. Existing coverage in packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/claudeCacheReview.test.ts:302-333 covers the engine. Validate with focused vitest runs for client-runtime and mobile plus typecheck of the touched packages.
decisionReason: This is a client-only latency change that reuses a mechanism already accepted and shipped for the web composer (609ac1563). It changes no auth, E2EE, relay or Hub protocol, or hosted lifecycle ownership. The advisory cost-guard trade-off (clearing on subscribed state, re-reading only flagged sends) was already decided for web; applying it to mobile is parity. Only the optional first-message title fold-in would need a server behaviour and compatibility decision, and it is not recommended as part of this item.
